constructs.name: Metaethical family
constructs.auditRationale: Metaethical family should remain a derived synthesis over independently measured metaethical commitments; MEI005 is diagnostic, not a standalone family scale.
constructs.coverageGap: A metaethical family combines independently interpreted answers; one diagnostic case cannot identify a family.

constructs.name: Liberty / opposition to domination
constructs.auditRationale: Liberty/opposition-to-domination is theoretically interesting, but it is not part of the standard MFQ-2 six-foundation model and the current items are original exploratory content.
constructs.coverageGap: The original domination items are not an administration of MFQ-2 or a calibrated foundation.

constructs.name: Knowledge complexity
constructs.auditRationale: Existing items directly ask whether knowledge is simple versus interconnected/developing; interpret only this narrow personal-epistemology proposition.

constructs.name: Attainability of truth
constructs.auditRationale: EPI015 was already excluded and the remaining material does not provide two independent negative indicators of truth attainability without conflating approximation, skepticism, and conventionalism.
constructs.coverageGap: The existing answer set confounds knowledge with certainty and domain-limited skepticism.

constructs.name: Rational / a priori reliance
constructs.auditRationale: Two direct, opposing items support a narrow a-priori-justification interpretation; EPI025 remains excluded as a knowledge/trivia recognition question.
constructs.coverageGap: New observation, all empirical support, and substantive knowledge differ; the existing pair is not converse evidence.

constructs.name: Scientific-method reliance
constructs.auditRationale: Public systematic testability can be interpreted as an epistemic preference, without claiming science is the only source of knowledge.

constructs.name: Revelation as epistemic source
constructs.auditRationale: Current items directly ask whether purported revelation can provide factual justification; this is distinct from revelation's moral or political authority.

constructs.name: External-world stance
constructs.auditRationale: The current construct conflates external-world metaphysics, perceptual directness, and skepticism. Retain narrower external-world-independence and skepticism interpretations; do not emit one categorical label.

constructs.name: Metaontology
constructs.auditRationale: Substantive-versus-deflationary attitudes can be reported, but framework relativity and verbalism should not be collapsed into one categorical metaontology label.
constructs.coverageGap: Substantive, framework-relative, and merely verbal disputes are different; the existing frequency claims do not align.

constructs.name: Identity under transformation
constructs.auditRationale: Identity-under-transformation is appropriately a derived pattern over continuity and transformation cases; one teleportation item cannot support a direct scale.
constructs.coverageGap: Transformation cases can inform a synthesis, but one teleportation scenario does not define a scale.

constructs.name: Free-will belief
constructs.auditRationale: Current free-will items partly encode compatibilist conditions, so disagreement may mean incompatibilism rather than disbelief in free will.
constructs.coverageGap: Compatibilist conditions cannot be used as denials of free will by incompatibilists.

constructs.name: Moral-responsibility belief
constructs.auditRationale: Current items directly address basic/desert-entailing responsibility and manipulation; keep distinct from forward-looking responsibility.
constructs.coverageGap: A manipulated action and causal explanation do not negate the possibility of desert in other actions.

constructs.name: Baseline human benevolence
constructs.auditRationale: The broad 'baseline benevolence' label overreaches. Existing direct items can support only the narrower claim that humans are capable of genuinely other-regarding motivation.
constructs.coverageGap: Capacity for altruism and frequency of benevolent action differ; disagreeing with often does not deny capacity.

constructs.name: Baseline human selfishness / competition
constructs.auditRationale: Self-interest prevalence and competition are different. Psychological egoism is already represented by AH13 and social competition by SO08; do not score this bundled construct as one worldview dimension.
constructs.coverageGap: Self-interest, psychological egoism, and competition are distinct claims; the current items bundle them.

constructs.name: Human-nature mutability
constructs.auditRationale: Existing items directly concern malleability of human dispositions; keep separate from whether causes are biological or environmental.
constructs.coverageGap: Change in some dispositions can coexist with stability in others; the apparent opposites have different quantifiers.

constructs.name: Human-nature complexity
constructs.auditRationale: A generic preference for multi-causal explanation is a methodological outlook with no clear validated worldview construct here; retain for research only.
constructs.coverageGap: Multicausal explanation is an exploratory methodological variable, not an interpreted human-nature factor.

constructs.name: Biological causal attribution
constructs.auditRationale: Interpret only the reported belief that biological/inherited factors can make substantial causal contributions; do not infer immutability or normativity.

constructs.name: Environmental / social causal attribution
constructs.auditRationale: Interpret only the reported belief that social/environmental factors can substantially shape behavior; do not infer blank-slate views.

constructs.name: Agency theory family
constructs.auditRationale: Compatibilist/libertarian/skeptical family classification must remain derived from free-will, determinism, and responsibility answers.
constructs.coverageGap: Freedom-theory families require joint free-will, determinism, and responsibility evidence.

constructs.name: Personal / agentic deity
constructs.auditRationale: Conditional questions directly distinguish personal/agentic from impersonal divinity; only interpret when relevant branch prerequisites are satisfied.

constructs.name: Divine / supernatural intervention
constructs.auditRationale: Current items directly address whether supernatural agency can intervene in ordinary events.

constructs.name: Miraculous intervention
constructs.auditRationale: Current items directly address miracles, while distinguishing unexplained natural events from miracle claims.

constructs.name: Revelatory authority
constructs.auditRationale: Current items support a narrow claim about purported revelation having authority for belief or conduct, distinct from public-law authority.
constructs.coverageGap: Overriding a purported revelation in one moral conflict does not deny all private revelatory authority.

constructs.name: Divinity model
constructs.auditRationale: Theism, deism, pantheism, panentheism, and impersonal divinity are a family of alternatives. Keep the family descriptive/derived rather than a single score.
constructs.coverageGap: Theism, deism, pantheism, and impersonal divinity are descriptive alternatives, not one direct scale.

constructs.name: Objective-purpose source
constructs.auditRationale: Designer-grounded and non-designer sources of objective purpose should be separate commitments, not one categorical score.

constructs.name: Existential nihilism
constructs.auditRationale: Current items directly distinguish denial of objective/inherent meaning from alternative objective or constructed sources.
constructs.coverageGap: A hypothetical without cosmic purpose cannot establish actual-world nihilism; nondivine objective meaning is another live view.

constructs.name: World safety
constructs.auditRationale: World-safety is a validated Primal World Beliefs construct, but these are custom items and should remain explicitly exploratory until calibrated.
constructs.coverageGap: World safety is an exploratory primal belief here; custom items are not a validated scale.

constructs.name: World aliveness / intentional character
constructs.auditRationale: World-aliveness is a validated primal family, but these custom items mix felt intentionality and metaphysical responsiveness; retain as research-only.
constructs.coverageGap: Perceived world responsiveness is exploratory and not evidence of a philosophical identity.

constructs.name: Optimism vs resignation
constructs.auditRationale: The current scale mixes social improvability, personal problems, and pessimism; it is not a clean optimism measure.
constructs.coverageGap: World-improvability items remain exploratory and uncalibrated.

constructs.name: Response to meaninglessness
constructs.auditRationale: Responses to meaninglessness should be derived from meaning/nihilism responses rather than scored as an independent latent trait.
constructs.coverageGap: Existential orientation combines separately interpreted propositions.

constructs.name: Relational / interdependent self
constructs.auditRationale: Existing items directly ask whether relationships/roles partly constitute identity; do not equate this with collectivism.

constructs.name: Tolerance of otherness
constructs.auditRationale: Interpret narrowly as toleration/noninterference toward disliked non-rights-violating ways of life, not generalized warmth toward outgroups.
constructs.coverageGap: Social health under diversity and willingness to accommodate are not the same as toleration.

constructs.name: Group-dominance preference
constructs.auditRationale: Current items align conceptually with group-dominance preference; custom wording is not an SDO-7 administration.

constructs.name: Anti-egalitarianism
constructs.auditRationale: Current items align with opposition to group equality as a distinct SDO-related tendency; do not infer explicit dominance.

constructs.name: Cooperation orientation
constructs.auditRationale: General cooperation preference is not equivalent to validated Social Value Orientation allocation behavior; retain for research.
constructs.coverageGap: Cooperation preference is not a Social Value Orientation allocation score.

constructs.name: Competition orientation
constructs.auditRationale: General competition preference is not equivalent to SVO or a single economic ideology; retain for research.
constructs.coverageGap: Competition preference is not a Social Value Orientation allocation score.

constructs.name: Scope of moral concern / cosmopolitan concern
constructs.auditRationale: Current items directly address moral scope across group boundaries; distinguish from institutional cosmopolitanism and absence of special obligations.

constructs.name: Social-category essentialism
constructs.auditRationale: Current items support a narrow psychological-essentialism interpretation; do not infer biological determinism or stereotype endorsement.
constructs.coverageGap: Natural regularity in a category does not imply a fixed essence; rare essence is not never essence.

constructs.name: Humanity-nature worldview
constructs.auditRationale: Humanity-nature worldview is hierarchical. Existing items support ecological interdependence and anthropocentric-priority subclaims, not one total ecological score.
constructs.coverageGap: Descriptive ecological interdependence and priority in welfare conflicts must not be one score.

constructs.name: Belief in social/world justice
constructs.auditRationale: Current items directly address general just-world belief; do not infer personal just-world belief or victim blaming.

constructs.name: Legitimacy of coercive political authority
constructs.auditRationale: Current items directly ask whether political institutions can possess a moral right to coerce; keep distinct from political obligation.
constructs.coverageGap: Rejecting automatic authority or performance alone leaves conditional political legitimacy open.

constructs.name: Centralization vs decentralization
constructs.auditRationale: Interpret as centralization/decentralization preference in stated governance contexts, not as a complete theory of federalism.

constructs.name: Distributive-principle family
constructs.auditRationale: Equality, need, desert, sufficiency, priority, and entitlement are different distributive principles. Ranking them does not justify one family score.
constructs.coverageGap: Equality, need, desert, sufficiency, priority, and entitlement need distinct propositions; rankings alone do not supply them.

constructs.name: Collective / common ownership legitimacy
constructs.auditRationale: Current items directly address legitimacy of common ownership; do not infer socialism or rejection of private property in all domains.
constructs.coverageGap: A private-property preference does not deny that some commons can be legitimate.

constructs.name: Collective / democratic coordination preference
constructs.auditRationale: Interpret as preference for participatory/democratic coordination in stated contexts, not as endorsement of political democracy everywhere.
constructs.coverageGap: Rejecting direction by a collective when exchange works does not endorse democratic authority.

constructs.name: Expert / administrative coordination preference
constructs.auditRationale: Interpret as preference for expert/administrative decision authority in stated contexts, distinct from valuing expert testimony.
constructs.coverageGap: Rejecting expertise alone as sufficient authority does not deny expert decision weight.

constructs.name: Deterrent punishment
constructs.auditRationale: Current items directly address deterrence as a purpose/justification of punishment; mixed theories remain possible.
constructs.coverageGap: Deterrence as one aim differs from deterrence alone justifying disproportionate punishment.

constructs.name: Rehabilitative / restorative punishment
constructs.auditRationale: Rehabilitation and restorative repair are distinct aims. Current direct items bundle them, so do not emit one combined score.
constructs.coverageGap: Rehabilitation and restorative repair are different purposes and are bundled in the current direct items.

constructs.name: Reform vs rupture orientation
constructs.auditRationale: Interpret as gradual reform versus decisive institutional replacement; do not equate rupture with violent revolution.

constructs.name: Ethical egoism as a normative principle
Ownness and revisable allegiance to ideals
Continuing endorsement and exit from commitments
Reliance-based reasons for performance or repair
Concepts as revisable instruments of inquiry
Easy or deflationary approach to ontology
Institutional and instrumental justification of rights
Territorial monopoly of final legal force
Contractual remedies distinct from continuing assent
